evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.1.35: clārē oculīs videō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The everyday word for seeing with the eyes, and also for seeing to something (vidē ut) and for understanding (see I get it). The passive videor is “seem” (see seem).

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. videō: syn. cernō
terms.comment: Seeing something distinctly, picking it out from what is around it; its perfect crēvī sounds like the perfect of crēscō, so in speech prefer vīdī.
Getting a sight of someone or something, often suddenly: “there he is!”

phrases.latin: phasēlus ille, quem vidētis, hospitēs, ait fuisse nāvium celerrimus
phrases.english: that boat you see, my guests, claims she was once the fastest of ships

phrases.latin: Oculus videt colōrēs, quid album vel ātrum, viride vel caeruleum, rubrum aut lūteum sit.
phrases.english: The eye sees colours, what is white or black, green or blue, red or yellow.
Can you see that ship? — Yes.
